title: Introduce hole-consolidator defragmenter and tenant-aware spill prioritizer
author: Ava Patel
release_notes: Adds a memory defragmenter (Hole Consolidator) and a tenant-aware spill prioritizer to reduce fragmentation-driven OOMs and to improve tail latency under mixed workloads. Opt-in via feature flag; safe to roll out incrementally.
description:
Context and motivation: In multi-tenant inference workloads we frequently see memory fragmentation in the KV cache leading to partial page allocations, increased spill volume, and higher tail latencies when large keys or long sequences are served. Existing eviction logic prefers LRU-ish heuristics which do not account for page-granularity holes and tenant importance, causing noisy neighbors to trigger unnecessary disk/GPU spillovers. This change introduces two cooperating subsystems: 1) a Hole Consolidator background pass that performs low-overhead, cache-local compaction to merge small free ranges into reclaimable pages; and 2) a Tenant-aware Spill Prioritizer that ranks spill candidates by a composite score (tenant SLA weight, page occupancy compaction benefit, estimated rebuild cost) and applies a backpressure multiplier when cluster-wide pressure spikes.

What this PR does (single-run description): Adds a compacting defragmenter that runs opportunistically during low-CPU windows, a spill-priority queue that surfaces high-value spill candidates, and the telemetry hooks to observe consolidation effectiveness. The algorithm is conservative by default and gated behind a feature flag (kv.hole_consolidator.enabled = false). Key behavioral rules: - Avoid moving hot pages (hotness determined by recent hit histogram and streaming KV TTL). - Merge adjacent free segments within the same allocation arena only to preserve allocation locality. - Prefer spilling pages that yield >25% reclaimable contiguous bytes. - Apply tenant-weight scaling so critical tenants are spared unless absolutely necessary.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc and microbench (ENG-11452) reviewed
- [x] Unit tests for allocator invariants
- [x] Integration tests with continuous batching harness
- [x] Telemetry events for consolidation/eviction counts
- [x] Feature flag + rollout plan

High-level commits in this PR: - initial: hole consolidator pass + scheduler integration - add: tenant weight model + spill scoring function - add: telemetry counters and per-tenant reclaim histograms - test: deterministic unit tests for corner cases (fragmentation boundary) - perf: microbench results and threshold tuning - docs: feature flag and rollout notes

Files/areas changed (high level): [src/serving/kv/allocator.cc, src/serving/kv/defrag_worker.cc, src/serving/kv/spill_prioritizer.cc, include/serving/kv/allocator.h, tests/kv/defrag_test.cc, infra/feature_flags.yaml, docs/kv/hole_consolidator.md, metrics/metrics_registry.cc]

Perf summary (internal bench): - Mixed-tenant replay (50 tenants, 20% heavy, 80% light) under steady state: peak fragmentation score reduced by 63% compared to baseline. - End-to-end tail latency (p95/p99) for long-sequence requests improved 14% / 21% respectively when consolidator enabled and prioritizer active. - Spill I/O volume dropped 38% over a sustained 30-minute spike test. - CPU overhead: background defrag consumed on average 2.8% of one core during low-load windows; configurable knob for throttle window provided.

Testing and CI: First CI run showed flaky failure in integration test kv_defrag_rebuild particularly on macOS runners (sequencing race). I pushed a fix to the synchronization and retried; second run passed all unit and integration jobs. Staging run on Dedicated cluster (canary) exercised feature flag for 72 hours and reported no regressions; metrics aligned with microbench.

Reviewer comments and author responses (flattened timeline): "Jonah Kim: Can the consolidator create temporary allocation spikes when coalescing multiple small holes?" -> "Author: We avoid allocating extra memory by doing in-place merges and only scheduling merges when contiguous free bytes exceed target; expanded explanation in allocator.h comments." "Lena García: Tenant weights need a safety cap to avoid starving best-effort tenants during sustained pressure." -> "Author: Added a decay-based cap and documented behavior; added ENG-11458 follow-up to refine policy per-customer." "Marcus Li: Please add an end-to-end test that simulates KV pages with interleaved references to ensure we don't accidentally double-free shards." -> "Author: Added defrag_test.cc with deterministic sequences and sanitizer-enabled CI job." "Lena García: approve with nits" -> "Jonah Kim: approved".

post_merge_notes: Feature is behind kv.hole_consolidator.enabled flag. Default remains off for existing clusters. Ops should enable on staging first and watch kv.consolidator.effectiveness and kv.spill.rate metrics. ENG-11458 will evaluate tenant caps after 2-week canary.
changelog: Performance: Reduce KV cache fragmentation and spill I/O via hole consolidation and tenant-prioritized spill; improves tail latency and reduces OOM risk under mixed workloads.
rollback_plan: Flip kv.hole_consolidator.enabled to false via feature-flag service (instant), and revert prioritizer with a targeted config change; document emergency-runbook in docs/kv/hole_consolidator.md.
notes_for_release_engineering: This is non-breaking and opt-in. Add metric dashboards to the 1.12.0 release monitor and include rollout steps in the release notes. Coordinate with SRE to schedule canary on low-traffic windows.
